title: MIG GPT: Harnessing Large Language Models for Automated Migration of Out-of-Tree Linux Kernel Patches Across Versions
abstract: MIG GPT is a framework that assists humans in automating the migration and maintenance of out-of-tree kernel patches across Linux kernel versions. It utilizes a novel code fingerprint structure to retain code snippet information and incorporates three modules to improve migration accuracy and efficiency.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're a developer trying to update a Linux kernel patch to work with a new version of the kernel. You'd have to manually analyze the differences between the old and new kernel versions, which can be time-consuming and error-prone. MIG GPT simplifies this process by leveraging large language models to automate the migration of out-of-tree kernel patches.

This is especially important for out-of-tree patches, which are not officially supported by the Linux kernel and require manual maintenance to ensure compatibility with newer kernel versions.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
MIG GPT works in two stages: identifying target code snippets in the new version and migrating the out-of-tree patch. It uses a code fingerprint structure to encode the structural features of code snippets, which enhances LLM performance and migration accuracy.

The code fingerprint structure records both the content and positional information for each line of statements, including comments and inline assembly.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
MIG GPT was evaluated on a robust benchmark consisting of three real-world projects from the out-of-tree patch community of the Linux kernel. The results show that MIG GPT significantly outperforms the direct application of vanilla LLMs, achieving an average completion rate of 74.07% (↑ 45.92%) for migration tasks.

The average number of queries to LLMs is only 2.26 (↑ 0.26), indicating no substantial increase in computational overhead.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
MIG GPT has significant implications for the development and maintenance of out-of-tree kernel patches. By automating the migration process, MIG GPT can save expert labor costs and reduce the development cycle.

This is especially important for projects that rely on out-of-tree patches, such as RT-PREEMPT, AUFS, and HAOC.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
MIG GPT introduces several key innovations, including the use of code fingerprints to retain code snippet information and the incorporation of three modules to improve migration accuracy and efficiency.

The retrieval augmentation module addresses challenge 1 and challenge 3, while the retrieval alignment module tackles challenge 2, and the migration augmentation module addresses challenge 4.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
MIG GPT is available on GitHub, and you can try it out on your own out-of-tree kernel patch projects.

Simply follow the instructions in the README file to get started.
